title: Every Banana You Eat Is Radioactive (Here's the Math)

scenes.text: Every banana you've ever eaten was radioactive.
Bananas are packed with potassium. And a tiny fraction of all potassium on Earth is potassium forty, a radioactive form as old as the planet.
One banana gives you about a tenth of a microsievert. Physicists even have a unit for it. The banana equivalent dose.
A whole truckload of bananas can set off the radiation alarms at shipping ports that hunt for smuggled nuclear material.
It's harmless because your body already holds far more potassium forty than a banana does. You are more radioactive than your lunch.
To get a dangerous dose, you'd have to eat roughly thirty-five million bananas at once. How many have you eaten so far?

description:
Every banana you have ever eaten was slightly radioactive.
Bananas are rich in potassium, and a tiny fraction of natural potassium is radioactive potassium-40. One banana delivers about 0.1 microsieverts, a unit physicists jokingly call the banana equivalent dose. A truckload can trip the radiation monitors at shipping ports.
It is harmless: your own body holds far more potassium-40 than a banana, and a dangerous dose would take around 35 million bananas at once.
How many bananas have you eaten in your life?
